why: The five units are the known solid sanity-krb5 failures of LU-20537 (test_10 'bad refcnt 1 on key', test_13 extra keys, test_152, test_200, test_201), seen identically on unrelated changes by two other uploaders (66081, 67591 and 68581 by one, 67074 by another) and fixed by LU-20543 (change 68440, leftover key on failed gss negotiation), which Rainshadow says this base 775afe5cead1 lacks. The patch only adds a krb5princ mount option and edits test_12/cleanup_12, which none of these steps exercise.

bugs.reason: One ambient cascade: a gss key left in the keyring by a failed negotiation (LU-20543) breaks the keyring refcount and count checks and then the later umount/mkdir; the same set fails together every time, on several uploaders' changes. Not the patch's.

notes: 'Only this uploader' is an artefact here: sanity-krb5 runs only under custom Test-Parameters, which essentially two uploaders (both working on gss) use, so a solid master failure looks confined. Rule idea: for suites run only via custom Test-Parameters, compute elsewhere over all changes that ran the suite regardless of the 30 day uploader window, and treat an open ticket naming the exact test list (LU-20537 here, shown as a suggestion) as ambient. Also test_10 was 'covered' by an accepted link yet still class patch; the confined flag should not override a link whose ticket shows other uploaders' changes.

why: Suite level FAIL with no failing subtest: the suite log runs every subtest to 'test complete, duration 2250 sec' and a clean cleanup (10 13 152 200 201 were excepted). The same empty suite fail hits sanity-krb5 on other changes, including a debug only change by another uploader (68695) and 66526/66527/67617, ticketed as LU-18511; the gss reconnect change has no visible link to it and the retest passed.

bugs.reason: One ambient suite level failure (LU-18511 family), both sessions show the same clean subtest run; not the patch.

notes: A '(suite fail)' with null error should never become patch-suspect from uploader confinement alone: the error is generic and the suite runs only on custom Test-Parameters of two uploaders. Require a failing step in the log before labelling suite fails as patch faults.

why: The patch adds sanity checks to the userspace llog_reader tool (plus sanity test_60j), neither of which ost-pools test_23b uses. The b2_15 session hung right after 'lctl conf_param lustre.quota.ost=none' while the cluster was still unstable from replay-single (repeated evictions and lost connections, a client OST write timing out and systemd-journald failing its watchdog on the client), a VM or environment stall; the retest passed and ost-pools timeouts also occur on lustre-master and master-next full runs.

bugs.reason: Single timeout from an environment stall after replay-single; not the patch.

notes: Timeout on a b2_15 change whose diff is a userspace utility not exercised by the suite: a rule that a TIMEOUT counts as patch-suspect only when the diff touches code the hung step runs (or the hang stacks point to touched code) would have cleared this. The 'other_changes 1' that made it confined is the same uploader's other change; with fleet timeouts present on master full runs the confinement is weak evidence for generic timeouts.

why: The crash log ends 'Kernel panic (not syncing): Out of memory: system-wide panic_on_oom is enabled' on a zfs server, the known osd-zfs OOM of LU-20276 (already linked and accepted). sanityn test_72 crashes the same way on at least 7 other changes in review-dne-zfs-part-5 and on master-next since 2026-08-22; the patch only changes lfs find (userspace liblustreapi and sanity tests), which sanityn test_72 does not run.

bugs.reason: Single ambient ZFS OOM panic (LU-20276); the session it retested crashed in sanityn test_70a with the same ticket.

notes: Covered by an accepted link to an open ticket with many changes, yet class patch because the 30 day elsewhere window counted only one other change. When an accepted ticket's own history spans many changes and branch runs (here master-next), the link should override the confined flag. A userspace-only diff (lfs/liblustreapi) cannot cause a server OOM panic; file-class reachability would clear this.

why: One zfs session where an OST was unusable for allocation: setstripe with explicit OST lists fails 'Remote I/O error (121)' (lod_qos turns ENOTCONN from an inactive OST into EREMOTEIO) in test_1b, 12, 16a, 16c, test_5 gets 'ost_idx 1 != 0', and test_15's last step finds no file with stripe_count=8 because the eof component got fewer stripes; all its earlier lfs find checks, the code the patch changes, passed. Neighbouring units in the same test set were labelled ambient, and the retest passed.

bugs.reason: One environment cascade in a single test set: an OST inactive for creates, so explicit OST placement and full width striping fail; the same cascade also produced test_1a, 1b, 12, 16b, 18, 20a, 20b, labelled ambient or single by Rainshadow.

notes: Rainshadow split one test set's cascade into patch and ambient units by per test history; all units of one failing test set that share a cause should get one verdict. A failure in a test that calls the patched tool (lfs find here) is not evidence when the failing check depends on layout creation and the tool's own checks pass. Also the patch is userspace only and the series sibling 68418 failed only from known ZFS OOM.

why: The folio conversion of the client IO path in ps53 corrupts reads: the sanity-flr test_38 client logs 'BAD READ CHECKSUM ... client 9c4a0c1d, server 2b3d0e71' then 'too many resent retries ... rc = -11', so the mirror resync cannot read a valid copy. The same signatures appear only on ps53 and on its three series descendants (67791, 65094, 68661) on the same day, and ps54 (two days later) passes 45 of 46 sessions with none of them.

bugs.description: All 57 units across sanity, sanity-flr, sanity-ec, sanity-hsm, sanity-pfl, sanity-sec, sanity-dom and sanityn: one core bug, a broken read data path in ps53
bugs.reason: Sampled logs show the same mechanism everywhere: client side BAD READ CHECKSUM and resend exhaustion (EIO/EAGAIN) under DIO reads, which fails 77d, 119c/m/q, 69, 78 and every lfs migrate, mirror resync, extend, split and merge (56xh/xi/xj, 56Ej, 272b, flr, ec, hsm 607, pfl 6, sec 59b, rc = 5); buffered reads return wrong page data (cmp differs at byte 8193 and 12289, page boundaries) in 44e, 155f/g/h and the sanityn/sanity-dom test_19 checksum mismatches; the 'log output exceeded 2500 MB' aborts are the checksum error flood. All vanish together in ps54.

notes: Correctly labelled; 'only this uploader' is real here because the series children carry this patch. Grouping rule: units whose error strings differ widely (cmp failed, migrate rc = 5, resync failed, readv failed, log too large) share one dmesg signature (BAD READ CHECKSUM), so grouping should key on dmesg or crash signatures, not test error text; one later patchset clearing every unit at once is good evidence of a single bug. Under labelling: the same ps53 sessions have about 150 more failures of this bug labelled ambient-no-ticket, known, unmatched or covered (sanity-ec 6b/6d/7a/12c/13/22a/23a/26a/28a/31e/34b resync and verify failures, sanity-flr 33b/34a/37/200a-c, sanity 56wa/56wc/56xg/119f/119p/155e/120b/120c, sanityn 16a/16j, sanity-quota 58, ost-pools 28, sanity-sec 52, and dbench failures in sanity-quota 8, sanity-pfl 8, replay-single 70b, lustre-rsync-test 2a). When a patchset fails nearly every session with one signature, units with generic or weakly ticketed errors in the same sessions should inherit the patch label.

why: The patch reworks server mount and MGS registration to start an MGS follower on every MDT/OST. In ps23 unmounting MDT0000 logs 'server_put_mount()) Can't find mount for MGS' and the remount then fails 'Unable to start osd on /dev/mapper/mds1_flakey: -114' (EALREADY); in ost-pools test_26 MDT0000 stays 'not available for connect (no target)' for over an hour until the session times out. All 61 sessions of ps23 failed (none passed) and nobody else hits these.

bugs.reason: One core bug: a target that held the MGS cannot be remounted after umount (MGS mount registration lost, osd start returns -114). Tests that restart mds1 fail with 'start mdsN failed' (17m) or 'Restart of mds1 failed' and the session then hangs until the timeout (replay-single 0a, recovery-small 23, replay-vbr 1b, sanityn 33d, ost-pools 26, large-scale cleanup); a suite setup that remounts everything fails with 114 then 17 or 32 on every target (sanity-quota, sanity-sec setup). The different timeout signatures per suite are just where each session was when mds1 was restarted.

Separate symptom in one ssk session: 'lctl conf_param -d lustre.srpc.flavor...' on the MDS node fails 'This command must be run on the MGS ... No such device' while MGCs get mgs_connect rc = -19 and config log timeouts, so sptlrpc rules cannot be removed ('still 2 rules left'); test_79 then fails umount after the client lost its mount. Probably rooted in the same MGS registration handling, but it fails through the follower refusing MGS ioctls rather than through the -114 remount, so a fix for the first group need not fix it.

notes: Labels are right, but the per suite 'Timeout occurred ... last suite running was X' signature splits one bug into six units; grouping should use the first failing step in the session (here the -114 restart of mds1). sanity test_27x and the sanity-sec suite fails on this patchset were labelled unmatched or ambient-no-ticket yet are in sessions where every server restart breaks; they were not checked in detail.

why: Every crash in ps31 is a NULL dereference on a server when a target is stopped or restarted: 'BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000018' in dt_locate_at, lu_object_find_at or ofd_object_find (sanity-hsm 26e, replay-single 0a, sanity-quota 7a/7b, conf-sanity 5h), and at 0x3d4 in tgt_discard_slc_lock from mdt_remote_blocking_ast (sanity-scrub 0), which takes mdt_dev(ls_top_dev). The commit message of later patchsets describes exactly this bug as fixed (mgs_fs_setup clearing ls_top_dev of the live MDT/OST so the next mdt_object_find or ofd_object_find crashes); all 33 sessions failed.

bugs.description: All 8 units (recovery-small 23, replay-single 0a, replay-vbr 1b, sanity-hsm 26e, sanity-pfl 9, sanity-quota 7a/7b, sanity-scrub 0): one bug
bugs.reason: The MGS follower setup on a shared lu_site leaves ls_top_dev NULL; any later object lookup or lock cancel through the top device oopses. The two crash sites (0x18 in object find, 0x3d4 in tgt_discard_slc_lock) differ only in which caller dereferences the NULL top device first.

notes: Cross suite 'node crashed during X' signatures here are one bug, and the crash site differs between units, so grouping by crash function would wrongly split it; grouping by the NULL top device (or by 'crash right after a target umount/mount on this patchset') would not. The same crash also hits insanity test_0, conf-sanity test_5h and sanity-ec test_30d on ps31, which Rainshadow labelled unmatched, covered or ambient-no-ticket and left out of the patch units: under labelling. ps31's crash is a different bug from ps23's -114 remount failure even though the same tests fail (recovery-small 23, replay-single 0a, replay-vbr 1b): unit identity across patchsets does not mean bug identity.
